title: Pseudo‑Classes: State & Position 🎭
description: Style elements based on user interaction, structural position, and negation.

slides.title: What Are Pseudo‑Classes? 🎭
slides.content:
# Keywords That Define State

A pseudo‑class is added to a selector to specify a special state of the selected element(s). Syntax:
```css
selector:pseudo-class { property: value; }
```
Examples:
- `:hover` – when the mouse is over the element.
- `:focus` – when the element has keyboard focus.
- `:nth-child()` – structural position among siblings.

They let you style dynamic interactions without JavaScript.

slides.title: Interactive Pseudo‑Classes 🖱️
slides.content:
# User‑Driven States

- `:hover` – mouse pointer over element.
- `:active` – element being activated (e.g., button being pressed).
- `:focus` – element has focus (keyboard navigation).
- `:focus-visible` – browser determines if focus indicator should be shown (often used to avoid focus ring on mouse clicks).
- `:visited` – link that has been visited.

```css
a:hover { color: red; }
button:active { transform: scale(0.98); }
input:focus { outline: 2px solid blue; }
```

quizData.question: Which pseudo‑class applies while a button is being clicked?
quizData.explanation: `:active` matches the moment the element is being activated.

slides.title: Structural Pseudo‑Classes 🏗️
slides.content:
# Target by Position Among Siblings

- `:first-child` – first child of its parent.
- `:last-child` – last child.
- `:only-child` – only child.
- `:nth-child(n)` – nth child (can use keywords `odd`, `even`, or formulas like `3n+1`).
- `:nth-last-child(n)` – count from the end.
- `:first-of-type`, `:last-of-type`, `:nth-of-type()` – same but only among siblings of the same type.

```css
li:first-child { font-weight: bold; }
tr:nth-child(even) { background: #f2f2f2; }
```

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## `:nth-child` vs `:nth-of-type`

`:nth-child` counts all children; `:nth-of-type` counts only elements of the same type. Use `:nth-of-type` when you want to skip over other elements like `<div>`s or headers.
